about.title: Placentia Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Placentia families rely on everyday products — vehicles driven along SR-57 and Orangethorpe Avenue, appliances at home, tools at job sites near Placentia Avenue — and expect them to work as intended. When a manufacturing flaw, design defect, or missing warning causes an injury instead, California law often lets the injured person hold the maker accountable without proving negligence. That's the heart of strict liability: show the defect, show it caused harm, and multiple parties in the supply chain may share responsibility. LawProactive isn't a law firm, but we connect Placentia residents free of charge with an independent attorney experienced in defective product claims. These attorneys typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless they recover compensation for you. If a product hurt you or someone you love in Placentia, keeping the item itself and any packaging can matter significantly for building a claim.

whyChoose.title: Why Strict Liability Matters for Your Placentia Claim

items.title: No Need to Prove Negligence
items.desc: Under California's strict liability standard, you generally don't have to show the manufacturer was careless — only that the product was defective and caused your injury.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Be Responsible
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially share liability, which may widen the paths available for recovering compensation.

items.title: Preserving Evidence Is Critical
items.desc: Because the defect itself is central to a strict liability claim, keeping the product, packaging, and any related documentation intact helps an attorney evaluate your case.

items.question: Do I have to prove the manufacturer was negligent to file a claim?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California's strict liability doctrine generally allows injured people to recover by showing a product was defective and caused harm, without needing to prove the company acted carelessly. This can simplify certain aspects of a product liability claim.

items.question: What should I do with the product that injured me in Placentia?
items.answer: Keep it exactly as it was at the time of the incident, including any packaging, manuals, or receipts. Physical evidence is often central to a product liability case, and an attorney can advise on proper preservation and documentation.

items.question: Are car parts or vehicles involved in Placentia crashes covered under product liability?
items.answer: Yes, defective vehicle components — such as brakes, airbags, or tires — can fall under product liability law even when the incident happens on roads like SR-57 or Orangethorpe Avenue. An independent attorney can help determine whether a vehicle defect contributed to a crash.

items.question: Is there a cost to get connected with an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: No, LawProactive's connection service is free. Attorneys in the network typically work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover compensation.
